title: Locked out, shut in, left hungry: Afghanistan after Taliban takeover
description: Since the Taliban's resurgence in Afghanistan, women's rights and access to education have suffered dramatically. Millions of girls are now prohibited from secondary and higher education, leading to dire social repercussions. In addition, food insecurity is rampant, affecting approximately 19.2 million individuals. The healthcare available has also significantly declined, obstructing women's ability to obtain necessary medical assistance. The overall humanitarian crisis continues to worsen, deeply affecting Afghan families' daily lives.

title: Why Trump's plan to unleash 'Mother Of All Bombs' may fall flat in Iran
description: Military discussions are considering the use of the MOAB against Iran's nuclear facilities and military targets. However, the effectiveness of the MOAB is limited against deeply buried sites protected by reinforced concrete. Analysts highlight that the GBU-57 penetrator is better suited for such underground facilities, which require specialized weapons for effective targeting. While the MOAB has a strong psychological impact, its military utility against hardened targets is questionable.

title: You earn, save & invest. Does that mean you're financially literate?
description: Financial literacy encompasses understanding one's income, expenses, and the risks associated with investments. Differentiating between saving and investing is crucial for effective financial planning. Individuals must be vigilant against financial fraud and misleading guidance in their investment choices. A well-structured financial plan aids in aligning savings and investments with personal objectives. Familiarity with financial concepts empowers individuals to make thoughtful decisions and manage their finances responsibly.

title: USCIS: Anyone who ‘guarantees’ a faster visa or Green Card is scamming you
description: USCIS warns immigrants and visa applicants about fraudulent schemes that promise quicker visa approvals in exchange for monetary fees. These scams frequently involve false claims of having special ties to government officials. USCIS insists that no one can hasten the immigration process through personal connections. Individuals should file applications independently and trust assistance only from recognized professionals. Recognizing fraudulent emails and suspicious offers is essential to protect against these scams.

title: Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law for $270,000; court rejects right to stay
description: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.
